### e5-counteroffensive-23 (Jun–Nov 2023)

The live reference for frontline geometry is DeepStateMAP [src:deepstate-map]. The monthly km² series is owned by topic 07 (see 07 §2.7). It is computed from DeepState's map versions [src:deepstate-api-history]:
- About 3,300 km² for 2024, against 3,600+ published.
- Net Russian gains of about 380–390 km² a month in e7–e8, falling to about 78 a month in e9.
- The grey zone roughly tripled, to about 1,600–1,800 km².

- **BTG** — battalion tactical group; Russia's 2022 combined-arms manoeuvre unit, largely dropped for regiments and divisions by 2023.
- **ZSU (Zbroini Syly Ukrainy)** — Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU).
- **TrO (Terytorialna oborona)** — Territorial Defence Forces.
- **DShV (Desantno-shturmovi viiska)** — Air Assault Forces; the core of the 2026 Oleksandrivka offensive.
- **SBU** — Security Service of Ukraine (ran Spiderweb).
- **HUR (Holovne upravlinnia rozvidky)** — Defence Intelligence of Ukraine.
- **Syly bezpilotnykh system (SBS)** — Unmanned Systems Forces.
- **LBZ (liniia boiovoho zitknennia)** — line of contact.
- **sira zona** — "grey zone", contested no-man's-land between positions.
- **kill zone / zona urazhennia** — the drone-saturated band near the front where any movement is observed and struck.
- **counterattack vs counteroffensive** — ISW's usage: a counterattack is a tactical action, while a counteroffensive is an operational-level undertaking like Kharkiv or Kherson in 2022. Ukrainian officials also avoided "counteroffensive" in Feb 2026.
- **"liberated" vs "restored control"** — Ukrainian official wording: the second covers grey-zone areas cleared of infiltrators rather than taken from full Russian control.
- **shturmovyky** — assault infantry.
- **miasni shturmy** — "meat assaults": Russian waves of expendable infantry (Wagner/Storm-Z style).
- **Storm-Z / Storm-V** — Russian penal assault units made up of convicts.
- **"beautiful reports" (Russian, as reported)** — Russian milblogger term for inflated reports of advances up the chain of command.
- **poias fortets** — "fortress belt": Sloviansk–Kramatorsk–Druzhkivka–Kostiantynivka.
- **KAB / UMPK** — Russian guided aerial bomb / the glide-and-correction kit that turns FAB dumb bombs into glide bombs.
- **Shahed / Geran-2 / Geran-3/4/5 / Gerbera** — Iranian-designed one-way attack drone and its Russian-built versions: piston engine, then jet; Gerbera is a decoy.
- **mopedy** — "mopeds": Ukrainian slang for Shaheds, after their engine noise.
- **perekhoplyuvach** — interceptor (drone), e.g. Sting.
- **FPV** — first-person-view kamikaze drone; **optovolokno** — fibre-optic-guided FPV, immune to RF jamming.
- **NRK (nazemni robotyzovani kompleksy)** — ground robotic systems / UGVs.
- **bavovna** — "cotton": ironic Ukrainian slang for explosions on Russian-held targets (from a Russian euphemism for blasts). This is the root of the game's name.
- **HIMARS / GMLRS** — US wheeled rocket launcher / its guided 227 mm rocket.
- **ATACMS** — US tactical ballistic missile fired from HIMARS/M270.
- **PAC-3** — the Patriot interceptor variant Ukraine relies on against Russian ballistic missiles.
- **Ramstein / UDCG** — the Ukraine Defense Contact Group donor forum.
- **PURL** — NATO's Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List: Europeans pay for US weapons (from Jul 2025).
- **Rubikon** — Russian elite Centre for Advanced Unmanned Technologies (drone interdiction unit); detail left to the drones file.

- **Rubikon strangles Ukrainian roads:**
  - Russia's Rubikon centre was sent to the Kostiantynivka area in April 2025 with long-range fibre-optic FPVs. Brigades had to rebuild their supply chains.
  - Net tunnels went up. Heavy bomber drones (*Kazhan*, "Bat") flew food, water, fuel and grenades around the clock, up to 20 runs per crew per day [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-kostiantynivka].
  - Rubikon grew from about 1,450 personnel (March 2025) to about 5,000 (spring 2026). Its stated mission includes hitting logistics and drone teams deep behind Ukrainian lines [src:fpri-2026-lee-putiata-rubicon].
- **Russian infiltration:** Assault groups shrank to 1–5 people creeping along treelines (*posadky*) [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-kostiantynivka]. Motorcycle groups ran 6–8 bikes (6–16 troops) with 2–3 EW sets and were also used for resupply and casevac. Ukrainian feedback says only about one in several groups survives [src:frontelligence-2025-motorcycle-assaults].
- **How Ukrainian attacks are now built** [src:rusi-2025-watling-combined-arms]:
  - FPVs work best from −3 to +3 km of the forward line.
  - UGVs evacuate wounded from 2–5 km out, at night, to medical posts 7+ km back.
  - Good units attack in seven phases over 5–10 days, taking 5–10% casualties against about 50% for uncoordinated attacks.
  - Russia systematically uses drones to find Ukrainian EW, radar, CPs and drone pilots.
- **MoD digital claims (September 2025):** Avengers classifies 70% of enemy vehicles in as little as 2.2 seconds, and Delta enables "up to 2,000 enemy assets neutralised per day" [src:mod-2025-delta-avengers-ecosystem].
- **Deep strike and counter-strike:**
  - Ukrainian refinery strikes peaked in August–October 2025 [src:carnegie-2026-vakulenko-refineries].
  - The SBU set off underwater charges at the Crimean Bridge piers on 3 June 2025 [src:wikipedia-crimean-bridge].
  - Russia hit Ukrainian rail almost 1,200 times in 2025, more than in 2023 and 2024 combined [src:kyivindependent-2026-hodunova-ukrzaliznytsia].
- **UGVs scale up:** 67 units used UGVs in November 2025, flying 2,900+ missions [src:mod-2026-ugv-9000-march]. Ukrainian road netting covered routes in five oblasts by October 2025 [src:euromaidanpress-2026-tril-net-tunnel-pace].
- **Satellite ISR diversifies after the March 2025 scare** [src:euromaidanpress-2026-ft-europe-intel] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-peoples-satellite]:
  - HUR runs its own platform for French CSO-3 imagery, under a deal signed in February 2025.
  - Japan shares SAR imagery with HUR, its first such sharing with any foreign state. Germany and Italy provide radar imagery.
  - NATO's APSS ("Aquila") pools data from 18 nations' satellites.
  - ICEYE (54 SAR satellites) has become the linchpin. A German-funded contract has supplied SAR data to the MoD since November 2024, and Rheinmetall–ICEYE plan to build satellites in Germany.
  - The crowdfunded "People's Satellite" had delivered 5,900+ SAR images to HUR by May 2026.
  - Budanov still said in December 2025 that Kyiv "remained critically dependent" on US satellite imagery and early warning. Macron's January 2026 claim that France supplies two-thirds of Ukraine's intelligence is disputed.
- **Russia's C2 software races to shorten its kill chain** [src:csis-2026-bondar-russian-c2]:
  - Unmanned systems carry out up to 80% of Russian fire missions.
  - The volunteer-built Glaz/Groza complex turns a one-click mark on a drone feed into a full fire-mission package for guns and mortars. It cuts detection-to-impact from hours to minutes.
  - Belousov announced the "Svod" tactical situational-awareness complex in August 2025, and an MoD council on a unified drone-management system met in September 2025. Earlier, a spyware-laced copy of the AlpineQuest mapping app had leaked Russian unit locations (early 2025).
- **Starlink on Russian mid-range drones:** from late December 2025, Rubikon and other units flew Starlink-equipped BM-35 and Molniya-2 drones deep into the Ukrainian rear. They hit trains and traffic on the E-50 highway, much like the battlefield air interdiction (BAI) that enabled their advances at Pokrovsk and Huliaipole [src:isw-2026-02-01-roca] [src:isw-2026-02-05-roca].

**Sub-phases.** The proposed split at about Aug 2025 holds up.
- **e8a, Mar–Aug 2025:** the Kursk pocket is lost, Russia makes its peak summer gains, Spiderweb, and Anchorage.
- **e8b, Sep 2025–Jan 2026:** the urban fight for Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad, the loss of Huliaipole, the Kupiansk counterattack, the 28-point plan, and Russia's Starlink-enabled mid-range drone interdiction from late December.

- **Operational deception worked:**
  - RUSI notes that Russian forces reliably committed resources against Ukraine's telegraphed moves and missed its concealed ones [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. That is the pattern of the loudly advertised Kherson push versus the Kharkiv breakthrough.
  - Russian battle-damage assessment was weak. Troops were not encouraged to report failures, and data was fused poorly between sensors.
  - Ukraine used decoys of prestige systems and false radio traffic. Russian cruise missiles hit dummy HIMARS in August 2022 [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons] [src:kyivpost-2023-decoys].
- **Russian HQs pushed back:** Ukrainian MLRS strikes in July 2022 drove Russian headquarters beyond 120 km from the front line. This caused serious friction through the autumn [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
- **Commercial SAR:** The "People's Satellite" was bought from $13.5 million crowdfunded in three days in June 2022 (the "People's Bayraktar" money, redirected when Baykar donated the drones). The ICEYE contract signed on 18 August 2022 gives one dedicated SAR satellite plus tasking across the constellation. Imagery reached HUR from September; it sees through cloud and at night, at up to 0.25 m resolution [src:euromaidanpress-2026-peoples-satellite].
- **Crimean Bridge (Kerch):** A truck bomb on 8 October 2022 dropped road spans and set fuel tank cars on fire. The road bridge was fully reopened only in February 2023 and the rail bridge in May 2023 [src:wikipedia-crimean-bridge].
## 4. Key-figures table
### e8-drone-kill-zone (Mar 2025 – Jan 2026)

- **bavovna (бавовна)** — "cotton". Ironic Ukrainian slang for explosions on Russian-held targets, mocking the Russian euphemism "khlopok" ("pop", a homophone of "cotton").
- **KAB (керована авіаційна бомба, kerovana aviatsiina bomba)** — "guided aerial bomb". Ukrainian shorthand for any Russian glide bomb (UMPK-kitted FAB).
- **UMPK** — Russian "unified gliding and correction module", a wing-and-GNSS kit bolted onto FAB bombs.
- **FAB** — Russian general-purpose high-explosive bomb (FAB-250/500/1500/3000, by kg).
- **arta (арта)** — slang for artillery. "Nasha arta" means "our guns".
- **prylit (приліт)** — "arrival". An incoming hit or impact.
- **vylit (виліт)** — "departure". An outgoing launch, also a sortie.
- **PPO (ППО, protypovitriana oborona)** — air defence.
- **mobilni vohnevi hrupy (мобільні вогневі групи)** — mobile fire groups. Truck-mounted machine gun or AA-gun teams hunting Shaheds.
- **mopedy (мопеди)** — "mopeds". Slang for Shahed/Geran drones, from the moped-like buzz of their engines.
- **shakhedy (шахеди)** — Shaheds. Used generically for Geran one-way attack drones.
- **tryvoha (тривога)** — air-raid alert.
- **kontrbatareina borotba (контрбатарейна боротьба)** — counter-battery fight.
- **Kropyva (Кропива, "nettle")** — Ukrainian artillery C2 and mapping software.
- **Hrim-2 / Sapsan** — Ukrainian ballistic missile programme.
- **Bohdana** — Ukrainian domestic 155 mm wheeled self-propelled howitzer.
- **lob / pitch-up fire** — helicopter or jet climbs and releases unguided rockets on a ballistic arc to stay out of MANPADS range.
- **reconnaissance-fire complex / reconnaissance-strike complex (RFC/RSC)** — Soviet and Russian concept of a sensor-to-shooter network; RUSI renders it "Reconnaissance Fires Circuit".
- **Strelets** — Russian reconnaissance-and-fire-control data system.
- **CRPA** — controlled reception pattern antenna, an anti-jam GNSS antenna.
- **FARP** — forward arming and refuelling point.
- **IADS** — integrated air defence system.
- **SEAD / DEAD** — suppression / destruction of enemy air defences.
- **GLOC** — ground line of communication: a road or rail supply route.
- **LMUR (Izdeliye 305)** — Russian light multipurpose guided missile for Ka-52M and Mi-28NM, about 15 km range.
- **armiiska aviatsiia (армійська авіація)** — army aviation: the Ukrainian helicopter branch, now also an anti-Shahed force.
- **CAP** — combat air patrol.
- **stand-off** — releasing a weapon from outside the enemy's air-defence envelope.

The front from Kharkiv to Kherson is mostly open steppe and forest-steppe farmland on chernozem (chornozem, "black earth"). Large fields are separated by planted windbreak belts, called *lisosmuhy* in Ukrainian (sing. *lisosmuha*) and *lesopolosy* in Russian [src:eou-shelterbelt] [src:cepa-2023-kallberg-treelines]. Natural woodland is scarce and occurs "mainly along rivers banks and in gullies" (balkas) [src:tarasov-usda-luhansk-wind-erosion]. The exceptions are the sandy pine forests on the left-bank terraces of the Siverskyi Donets (Lyman, Kreminna and Serebrianka) [src:wikipedia-siverskyi-donets] [src:kyivindependent-2022-ponomarenko-donbas-woods]. The Donbas adds mining towns with terrikons (spoil heaps) 40 m to over 100 m high, coke and chemical plants, and Soviet apartment blocks [src:euromaidan-2023-havrylets-avdiivka] [src:euromaidan-2024-toretsk-highrises].

Research notes for *bavovniatko*. Scope: intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR); command and control (C2); and logistics in the Russo-Ukrainian war, 2022 to September 2026. We look at it from the Ukrainian side. Russian capabilities are described as Ukrainian and Western sources report them. Inline source tags point to `sources/05-isr-c2-logistics.yaml`.

Research note for *bavovniatko*. The player is always the Ukrainian side. Accessed 2026-09-28 to 2026-09-30. Citations are inline src-id tags in square brackets, resolved in `sources/00-timeline-eras.yaml`. Claims attributed to one side are marked as such, and contested numbers are given as ranges with who claims what.

**What Ukraine had.** By summer 2022 Ukraine had used up its own stocks of most critical munitions and depended on partners [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **155 mm tube artillery.** The US delivered 187+ M777s from April 2022 onward, with Excalibur guided shells. Its total of 155 mm howitzers eventually passed 200 [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine] [src:state-2025-us-security-cooperation-ukraine].
- **HIMARS.** The first four were in Ukraine by 24 Jun 2022 and a second four were due by mid-July [src:kyivindependent-2022-himars-arrive]. British M270s followed from July [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine].
- **Effect.** Western precision fires hit Russian logistics in **June–July 2022** and took away Russia's advantage of massed artillery supplied from rail-fed depots [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

## 3. Other maps compared

- **Excalibur bottomed out.** It hit the target only 6% of the time by August 2023 [src:kyivpost-2024-chiu-gps-weapons].
- **Ukrainian drone use depended on Russian EW.** If Russian EW was active, UAVs "could not get in" [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak].
- **Jamming as a tell.** Russian aviation strikes were heralded by the *lifting* of Russian GPS jamming, an exploitable signature [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak].
- **Russian EW adapted to being hunted** [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak]:
  - Zhitel used more subtly.
  - Antennas dispersed on light platforms.
  - Pole-21 treated as expendable wide-area cover.
  - Shahed navigation hardened.
  - Krasukha-4 hidden under nets in forest belts. Drones still found one near Urozhaine in November 2023, only the second recorded loss of the type [src:militarnyi-2023-kushnikov-krasukha-4-zaporizhzhia].
- **The EW gap in numbers.** Zaluzhnyi's November 2023 essay counts about 60 types of modern Russian EW against Ukraine's mostly Soviet-era kit. It names Pokrova as a nationwide GNSS spoofer that could deny satellite navigation over most of Ukraine [src:euromaidan-2023-voichuk-economist-ew].
- **Cope cages** *(mangaly)* **appeared on Russian tanks** from mid-2023 [src:kyivpost-2024-turtle-tanks].

## 7. Key figures

**ISR.**
- Orlan-10 and Zala drones at operational depth; five orbits over each axis; Lancet and FPVs doubling as scouts [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
- Rubikon is Russia's centralised drone centre for new tactics and deep interdiction. By 2026 it had 17 detachments of about 474 people each, with FPV, fixed-wing FPV, Lancet/Supercam, Orlan and counter-UAS/EW teams [src:fpri-2026-lee-putiata-rubicon].
# 01 — Drones and uncrewed systems

**Key battles and operations.**
- **Kharkiv counteroffensive** from **6 Sep 2022**: Balakliia (8 Sep), Izium and Kupiansk (10 Sep), Lyman (1 Oct). Ukraine claimed about 12,000 km² and 500+ settlements. ISW assessed about 2,500 km² for the breakthrough phase alone [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive]. The Russian Western Group of Forces collapsed [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Kherson:** Ukrainian fire control over the Dnipro crossings forced an orderly Russian withdrawal from the right bank in Oct–Nov 2022. Kherson city was liberated in November [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons] [src:wikipedia-russo-ukrainian-war].

Notes:
- **Assessed vs claimed.** ISW's two epistemic tiers ("assessed" = evidence-backed, "claimed" = asserted but unverified) are the clearest model of *confidence as a map layer*. In the web-map JSON:
  - Russian-controlled terrain and Russian advances share a translucent red fill (RGBA 239,0,0,71) with a red outline.
  - Infiltration areas are a patterned picture-fill with a **dashed** red outline.
  - Claimed Russian territory is translucent orange (255,170,0,126).
  - Claimed Ukrainian counteroffensives are translucent light blue (115,223,255,147) with a blue outline [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain].
  - The infiltration feature service was created on 20 December 2025 (e8) [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain].
- **ISW methodology:**
  - Each daily ROCA pairs a theatre map with per-sector zoom maps. The text runs axis by axis, each with a stated "Russian objective" and the "assessed objective" of named Russian armies. Control changes are backed by "geolocated footage published on" a given date, and every report ends with the note that ISW "uses only publicly available information" and receives no classified material [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
  - Earlier ROCAs (seen only in search excerpts in pass 1) state that the map shows "the furthest assessed extent of Russian advances" until open-source evidence shows otherwise, that this may underestimate Ukrainian advances, and that a porous front complicates control of terrain.
- **Partisans.** ISW keeps two partisan products: "reported but not confirmed Ukrainian partisan warfare" (feature service, 2022–) and a curated "Verified Ukrainian Partisan Attacks" StoryMap that only includes high-confidence events [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain].
- **Reputation of the one-person maps** is contested and only documented in Wikipedia editors' discussions. Suriyak was ruled unreliable for anonymity and unclear method (2021), then split editors between "partisan" and "very neutral… among the more conservative sources" (2024). One editor's 2024 ranking put ISW first, DeepState and Andrew Perpetua tied second (Perpetua "mostly based on geolocated footage… a bit cautious in reporting Russian gains"), and Suriyak, MilitaryLand, Rybar and Liveuamap lower. [src:wikipedia-rsn-2024-suriyakmaps] [src:wikipedia-talk-2024-territorial-control-mappers]. Perpetua's page carries a fundraiser for Ukraine's Khartiia corps [src:perpetua-ukrdailyupdate-map]. Treat all three as low-to-medium, single-team sources.
- **AMK's legend is a close relative of DeepState's.** It uses the same Google-palette reds and blues (`#A52714` for Russian control, `#0288D1` for Ukrainian advances) and adds explicit *advance* layers and a black infiltration zone. That is the "change this period" layer DeepState only implies with its two-week blue [src:amk-mapping-control-map].
- **Liveuamap icon semantics.** The site does not document its legend. In a captured feed, each event carries a code of the form pictogram-colour index: Russian strikes are `shahed-1`, `bomb-1` and `destroy-1`; Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia, explosions in Kursk, Ukrainian air defence, casualties in Ukraine and Zelensky statements are `drone-2`, `explode-2`, `aa-2`, `medicine-2` and `speech-2`; a US Congress item is `speech-10`. The page loads red, blue, green, white and black icon sets. The reading "1 = red = Russian, 2 = blue = Ukrainian" is an inference from 19 events [src:liveuamap-home-2026-09].
- **GeoConfirmed's icon grammar** is the most game-ready. Every object type has three states: active, "recently destroyed/damaged [visible in footage]" and "older destroyed". Colour is the faction *doing* the act ("colour of who is shelling"; a killed civilian is drawn "in the colour of who is assessed as doing the attack"; brown = UXO). Types range from tanks, APCs and trucks to suicide and multipurpose UGVs, short- and long-range one-way attack drones, interceptions, trenches, mines and CBRN incidents. Faction colours for Ukraine: Ukraine `#0051CA`, Ukraine civilian `#3184FF`, Russia `#E00000`, Russia civilian `#FF6666`, North Korea `#6A1D00`, Belarus `#400080` [src:geoconfirmed-openapi].
- **Black Bird Group on control:** "When we paint an area as Russian or Ukrainian-controlled, it's more like here the Ukrainians or Russians generally have more control than the other side." It also values being able to say its map is based on open sources [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping].

Vehicles and logistics inside the band suffer attrition every turn unless they are dug in, move at night or are escorted by EW.
- **Split the band by link type.** A political event (the Starlink cut-off) removed Russia's satellite-linked deep layer but left its fibre layer intact. Biletsky's 20–40% effectiveness drop, with partial recovery over one to two months, is a usable event curve [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment][src:kyivindependent-2026-post-starlink-scramble].
- **The EW vs link-type triangle.** RF FPVs are cheap but jammable, with a 60–80% failure rate (RUSI) or 10–15% success (CSIS) [src:rusi-2025-watling-reynolds-third-year][src:csis-2025-bondar-ai-autonomy]. Fiber drones cannot be jammed but have limited range and snag risk. In frost, ice stops spools unwinding and iced cable snaps, so range and link reliability should fall with temperature [src:euromaidan-2026-kossov-icy-fibre]. AI terminal guidance raises success to a claimed 70–80% in the last metres [src:csis-2025-bondar-ai-autonomy]. Satellite links (Starlink) extend reach but can be revoked, as in February 2026 [src:kyivindependent-2026-starlink-catastrophe]. The USF's 360,000 targets hit in 1.7m sorties (about 1 in 5) is a sanity check on aggregate rates [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-brovdi-102000].
- **Production and budget economy.** Drones are a consumable throughput resource, measured in millions per year [src:pravda-2025-hubina-3m-fpv], rather than a unit roster. Cost asymmetry drives air defence: a $2k interceptor against a $20–50k Shahed [src:csis-2025-jensen-drone-saturation][src:defenceexpress-2025-sting-effectiveness], and jet Gerans reset that balance [src:united24-2026-place-jet-gerans]. A reusable bomber at $8,500 for about a dozen sorties is cheaper per mission than one-use FPVs [src:euromaidan-2026-axe-bomber-drones].
- **Strategic-strike pressure curve.** The quarterly Shahed series (about 400 in Q4 2022, about 1,300 in Q4 2023, about 6,300 in Q4 2024, about 16,000 in Q4 2025) can drive the Russian strategic-strike track. The Air Force's shot-down share is also a ready-made air-defence difficulty setting: over 90% early, falling as volumes and jets rise [src:kaggle-2026-ivaniuk-missile-attacks][src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly].
- **E-points as an in-game currency.** Verified kills uploaded to DELTA earn points that units spend in a Brave1 Market catalogue [src:digitalstate-2025-brave1-epoints]. This maps directly to a player economy, including the moral hazard of chasing points. The programme survived a change of defence minister [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-dot-chain-500-units].
- **Robots replacing people in the kill zone.** UGV logistics and casevac can remove soldiers from the last 10 km; the monthly mission curve for 2026 is a ready-made tech-adoption curve [src:united24-2026-ugv-missions]. Late-game options include UGVs air-dropped by heavy bombers [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-vivaldi-ugv-drop].
- **Counter-drone units as priority targets.** Rubikon-style units should AI-target the player's drone teams, EW and supply routes rather than infantry [src:rferl-2025-rubicon]. Destroying their operators and launch sites should degrade Russian drone density across a sector [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-rubicon-vivaldi].
### e7-kursk-pokrovsk (Aug 2024–Mar 2025)
### e6-avdiivka-attrition (Oct 2023–Jul 2024)

**What Ukraine had.**
- **Force.** The plan called for 12 armoured and mechanised brigades on a 30 km frontage, Tokmak isolated in 7 days, then Melitopol. In the event only a couple of brigades were properly equipped, and most were newly raised and undertrained [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Fires.** At most 55 guns of 155 mm fired on the main axis, at about **70 rounds/gun/day at peak and as low as 10**. There were about **7 GMLRS a day** for the whole theatre [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Missiles.**
  - Over **300 Storm Shadow/SCALP** arrived during the offensive, SCALP from July [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons] [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine].
  - **ATACMS** were first used on **17 Oct 2023**: the 165 km cluster-munition variant, delivered secretly days earlier, against the Berdiansk and Luhansk airfields [src:isw-2023-10-17-roca].
- **Late arrivals.**
  - The first **Abrams** arrived on 23 Sep 2023 (confirmed by Zelensky on 25 Sep), out of 31 in total. They came too late for the offensive [src:isw-2023-09-25-roca] [src:state-2025-us-security-cooperation-ukraine].
  - M117 demining vehicles were usable only from Oct 2023 [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**Key battles and operations.**
- **Avdiivka**, from 10 Oct 2023 until Syrskyi announced the withdrawal on the evening of 17 Feb 2024. The Tavria commander claimed almost 50,000 Russian losses in the battle (Ukrainian claim) [src:euromaidanpress-2024-tril-avdiivka].
- After that, Russia began its slow drive west towards Pokrovsk, covering about 50 km from Feb 2024 to Jan 2026 at about **70 m/day** [src:csis-2026-jones-10-charts].
- The **northern Kharkiv offensive** from 10 May 2024 (Vovchansk, Lyptsi) stalled at about 10 km depth. On 30 May 2024 Washington allowed US weapons to be used against targets in Russia near Kharkiv [src:wikipedia-2024-kharkiv-offensive].

- **The CRPA ladder climbed.** Russian CRPA went to 12 elements on UMPK (April 2025) and 16 elements on Shahed and Iskander-K [src:defenseexpress-2025-kometa-m-16]. A new series of Russian CRPA resists more jammers than it has elements, which made KABs effective again until Lima-Quant (see e9) [src:forbes-2026-hambling-lima-quant].
- **Ukraine hunted jammers directly.** It tested EW-hunting FPVs in April 2025 [src:militarnyi-2025-kushnikov-ew-hunter-fpv] and fielded the networked Atlas EW system in July 2025 [src:defensepost-2025-encarnacion-atlas].
- **Frequencies spread out.** One sector showed a 20% / 30% / 50% split across the 400 MHz, 900 MHz and 2.1–2.3 GHz bands [src:pravda-2025-fpv-ew-shield].
  - Captured Russian chips cover 300–1100 MHz, so Ukrainian units pre-order jammers for bands the enemy can reach by firmware update.
  - Dome jammers protect 200–300 m; directional ones reach several km.
  - Trench EW weighs 20–50 kg plus a generator.
  - Russian ELINT satellites map Ukrainian emitters.
  - Kvertus says 6,000 Mirage nodes and 300 Azimuth receivers would cover the 1,300 km front for over UAH 5bn; only 10% was funded.
  - Industry sources agree drones "hold the initiative" and blame the institutional speed of deployment, not technology.
- **Big vehicle EW pulled back.** Bukovel-AD, Nota, Ai-Petri, Damba and Beton were forced back from the front by longer-range drones and fibre. One commander compares them to helmets: "potentially lifesaving … but offering no guarantees" [src:euromaidan-2025-zoria-jamming-fails].
- **Fibre: Russia ahead, Ukraine catching up.** Ukraine had about 1 in 10 teams on fibre by May 2025 [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-fiber-optic].
- **Nets became infrastructure.** Russia built net tunnels in February 2025 [src:defenseexpress-2025-russian-net-tunnels], and Ukraine followed in Zaporizhzhia from September 2025 [src:euromaidan-2025-murdoch-net-tunnels].
- **Improvised counters to fibre drones** [src:united24-2025-barkhush-fiber-counters]:
  - Tungsten "hot wire" that snaps the cable.
  - Shotgun teams.
  - Net guns.
  - Nets, with the caveat that "waiting" drones *(zhduny)* can hide under them.
- **Thermal masking.** Russian groups tried anti-thermal ponchos at the dawn changeover between thermal and day drones (May 2025). They reduced thermal contrast only partly, and movement gave the men away [src:militarnyi-2025-yan-russian-thermal-ponchos].
- **Autonomy went to mass production.** TFL-1 terminal autonomy entered mass production in September 2025 [src:kyivpost-2025-orlova-tfl1].
- **Interceptors turned on Shaheds.** Interceptor drones scored their first Shahed kills in early 2025, and Russia fielded its own interceptors from mid-2025 [src:kse-2025-drone-innovations].
- **Gun air defence.** Skynex batteries (four towed 35 mm guns with AHEAD airburst, about 4 km range) shot Shaheds over point targets [src:militarnyi-2025-shumlianskyi-skynex-shaheds]. Gepard remained "one of the key" AA guns, and Ukraine began repairing them at home in August 2025 [src:militarnyi-2025-gepard-repair].
- **Drones dominate the front.** 80–85% of frontline targets were engaged by drones [src:kse-2025-drone-innovations].
- **Russian mesh began.** Russian mesh networks for Geran control were documented in 2025 at about half their 2026 range [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-mesh-175km]. Ukrainian radio makers moved to mesh too: four Himera handhelds gave one brigade 45 km of signal across forest [src:euromaidan-2026-kossov-himera-mesh].

- **Artillery.** Ukrainian M777 batteries normally had to displace 2–15 min after opening fire. Ammunition hoarded for the offensive allowed a short "freedom to fire" [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak].
- **Helicopter "artillery".** The Ka-52 firing Vikhr and Ataka ATGMs was the leading aviation threat. Mi-35M added Ataka and lofted S-8 salvos. Strikes came from 8–10 km, often with an EW-escort helicopter. Ukrainian troops learned that when Russian GPS jamming lifted, attack helicopters were coming [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak]. Around Robotyne the UK MoD called the Ka-52 "one of the most influential Russian weapons systems" against the offensive. It flew at 50–100 m and carried up to 12 Vikhr ATGMs (about 8 km). The new Ka-52M added the LMUR (Izdeliye 305), with about 15 km range and a 25 kg warhead, well beyond the roughly 6 km reach of a Stinger [src:elpais-2023-ka52-counteroffensive]. Ukrainian MANPADS teams still got some: the 47th Mechanised Brigade claimed its eighth Ka-52 near Robotyne on 17 Aug 2023, with a single launch [src:ukrinform-2023-ka52-robotyne]. Oryx has 69 Ka-52 losses confirmed over the whole war [src:oryx-russian-losses].
- **Russian doctrine change.** Russia dropped the Soviet norm of about 720 rounds to suppress a platoon position. It prioritised Krasnopol production and brought in Lancet-3M: "effect over volume" [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak].
- **Glide bombs** were already a significant factor on the Zaporizhzhia front in summer 2023 [src:japcc-2026-zanier-glide-bombs].
- **Ukrainian deep strike.** Storm Shadow, fired from Su-24M since May 2023, hit the Chonhar bridges and, on 22 Sep 2023, the Black Sea Fleet HQ in Sevastopol [src:wikipedia-storm-shadow]. The first ATACMS strikes (October 2023) destroyed helicopters on occupied airfields [src:wikipedia-atacms]. The GBU-39 SDB (small-diameter bomb), delivered from November 2023, hit about 90% of the time [src:stripes-2024-khurshudyan-jamming].

- **Russian assault style.** Battalion-level mechanized waves. Satellite imagery shows 109 vehicles lost from 10 to 20 October 2023, about 200 according to ground sources. Once the armour failed, the infantry went in on foot [src:frontelligence-2023-avdiivka-losses]. Storm-V units fought at Avdiivka [src:ukrpravda-2024-isw-storm-v]. "Turtle" (shed) tanks appeared in April 2024 at Krasnohorivka, with mine rollers and EW. They absorb FPVs but are nearly blind, and their turrets cannot traverse [src:wikipedia-turtle-tank].
- **Ukrainian defence.** Ukraine defended with mines, artillery (short of shells) and FPVs. The April 2024 mobilization law lowered the call-up age from 27 to 25 and dropped demobilization after 36 months [src:rferl-2024-mobilization-law].
- **Vovchansk (from May 2024).** Russia's cross-border push into northern Kharkiv Oblast turned into an urban fight for Vovchansk. By July over 200 Russians had been besieged in the reinforced aggregate plant for more than a month and were kept alive by drone resupply. Ukraine chose bombardment over assault, and its drones destroyed dozens of excavators digging Russian trenches [src:euromaidan-2024-rfu-vovchansk-aggregate].

## 7. Terms

- **e1:** A pre-war professional army of BTGs with contract soldiers, VDV spearheads and huge artillery parks (2,433 barrel systems and 3,547 MLRS). It planned a 10-day campaign. Logistics and C2 failed, and the force was too small for the frontage [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **e2:** Russia reverted to what it does well: rail-fed massed artillery, a 10:1 fire advantage and slow city-by-city advances. Volunteers took the brunt of Russian dead from mid-2022 [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons] [src:mediazona-2026-casualties-count].
- **e3:** After Kharkiv exposed the manpower shortage, Russia mobilised 300,000, pulled back behind the Dnipro and began building the Zaporizhzhia lines. It started a war economy from May 2022 [src:wikipedia-2022-russian-mobilization] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. The Iranian Shahed arrived in Aug–Sep 2022 [src:csis-2026-bondar-shahed-geran].
- **e4:** **Wagner and the convict conveyor.**
  - Prisoners were the largest category of named dead by Mar 2023, and 88% of Wagner's Bakhmut dead were convicts [src:mediazona-2026-casualties-count] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - Trained Wagner troops lost only about 40–60 a week, and convicts were treated as disposable fixing forces [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - The army moved back from BTGs to divisions and regiments, padded with Storm-Z units [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **e5:** A textbook prepared defence. Three belts, regiments rotated to stay fresh, 35 days of cached ammunition, Lancets and helicopters, and early glide bombs [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. Wagner mutinied in June 2023 [src:wikipedia-russo-ukrainian-war]; its fate after the mutiny is left to the manpower file.
- **e6:** Industrial-scale glide bombs (about 40k UMPK in 2024). DPRK shells shored up ammunition supply, and Russia's shell advantage was 5:1 or more. Shahed volume grew but early interception rates were high [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year] [src:wikipedia-north-korean-involvement] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka] [src:csis-2026-bondar-shahed-geran].
- **e7:** A **volunteer/contract model** replaces mobilization.
  - Recruitment was 400k+ in 2024, and was expected to keep exceeding losses of 1,200+ casualties a day [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year]. Bonus structures are left to the manpower file.
  - Volunteers are again the largest category of Russian dead from Sep 2024 [src:mediazona-2026-casualties-count].
  - North Korean troops appear in Kursk, and Russia's armoured-vehicle stocks from storage were running down [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].
- **e8:** Drone-centric, infantry-infiltration warfare.
  - Fibre-optic FPVs, 50,000+ Shaheds a year and 70k UMPK ordered [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year] [src:csis-2026-jones-10-charts].
  - Recruitment met its 403,000 plan (HUR) [src:euromaidan-2025-murdoch-budanov-403k].
  - Up to half of Russia's artillery ammunition may be North Korean (Ukrainian intelligence claim) [src:wikipedia-north-korean-involvement].
  - Migrants and vulnerable groups are coerced into service [src:wikipedia-2022-russian-mobilization].
  - Late in the era, Russian drone units used Starlink to extend mid-range strikes on the Ukrainian rear [src:isw-2026-02-01-roca].
- **e9:**
  - **C2.** The loss of Starlink and throttled Telegram hurt Russian C2 [src:isw-2026-02-12-assessment] [src:united24-2026-litnarovych-starlink].
  - **Summer offensive.** In early February Russia was struggling to seize the start lines for its planned summer 2026 offensive, towards Sloviansk–Kramatorsk and/or Orikhiv–Zaporizhzhia. The southern counterattacks set it back further [src:isw-2026-02-15-roca].
  - **Losses exceed recruitment.** Losses stay at about 32,800 a month (General Staff) while gains shrink to about 290 casualties per km² [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km]. Syrskyi and the unmanned-systems commander Brovdi say losses now outrun recruitment [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-syrskyi-march].
  - **"Beautiful reports."** ISW and Russian milbloggers describe a culture of inflated reports that misleads Putin and set up Vivaldi's surprise [src:isw-2026-09-06-roca] [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
  - **Strike arsenal.** It moves to jet Gerans (Geran-4/5), with ballistic missiles aimed at the Patriot gap [src:militarnyi-2026-jet-geran-interceptors] [src:csis-2026-bondar-shahed-geran] [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
  - **Conscription** becomes year-round [src:wikipedia-2022-russian-mobilization].
  - **Oil revenue.** The Iran war's oil spike cushions Russia's budget [src:kyivpost-2026-struck-feshchenko-oil-windfall].

  - Mid leg: nets, night movement, fast vehicles.

- FPV — first-person-view drone, flown via goggles; usually a one-way strike drone.
- Dropper / bomber — a multirotor that drops munitions (e.g., Vampire, Baba Yaga) rather than diving in.
- Loitering munition — a drone munition that searches before striking (e.g., Lancet, Shahed-type).
- Shahed — Iranian-designed long-range one-way attack drone used by Russia; the target of interceptor sims.
- EW — electronic warfare: jamming, spoofing, direction finding.
- RSSI/LQ — received signal strength / link quality; the drone-link health measures used in the Arma mod.
- Kill zone — the ~10+ km band near the front where drones make vehicle movement lethal.
- ISR — intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance.
- ADB / ePoints — Army of Drones Bonus, a points-for-verified-strikes programme.
- DELTA — Ukraine's situational-awareness system; strike videos are verified there.
- Brave1 Market — Ukrainian defence marketplace where units spend ePoints.
- WeGo — simultaneous-turn system (Combat Mission) where both sides plot, then execute together.
- OOB — order of battle.
- CPX — command post exercise; staff training driven by a simulation.
- Matrix game — argument-based adjudicated wargame, common in professional gaming.
- KShVI — Russian command-staff military games (procedural rehearsal).
- P500 — GMT's preorder system; a game goes to print after 500 orders.
- PvPvE — players fight each other and AI at the same time.
- Double-blind — neither side sees the other's forces except through reports.
- Goodhart's law — when a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring what matters.
- Sense-and-strike complex (recon-strike complex) — the linked sensors, C2 and fires that find and hit targets within minutes; the thing Canadian games found hardest to break.
- Loitering ammunition — Broken Arrow's term for its planned one-way attack munitions (missiles with man-in-the-loop or AI terminal guidance).
- Chaika / Chaika-M ("Seagull" / "Flyswatter") — Ukrainian VR air-defence simulators codified by the MoD in 2025.
- RTCA — "real-time command action", Hell Of War's label for a command-drone view with drop-in direct control.
- SOP — standard operating procedure; in Flashpoint Campaigns, standing rules that units follow between orders.

- **CSIS wargames on Russia–Ukraine or NATO–Russia**: not found. csis.org returns 403. The archived Futures Lab page lists Ukraine analysis (an energy-truce piece) but no Russia–Ukraine wargame, and PAXsims only references CSIS's Taiwan games. The NATO–Russia games that were found are German, British and Canadian (§5).
- **Dstl on Ukraine drone lessons**: the gov.uk search API found only the Dstl–Slitherine case study, the Defence Wargaming Centre pages and a strategic-communications game (Defending Defender). No Ukraine drone game was public.
- **Commercial FPV sims in Ukrainian schools**: no first-party source names Liftoff, VelociDrone, Uncrashed or DCL. Searches of Euromaidan Press's archive for each name found nothing. Only the vendor claim [src:vgi9-2025-drone-simulators] remains, and the verified military sims are all domestic.
- **Combat Mission: Black Sea community mods** for FPV or 2022 content: the Battlefront forums returned 403. Official content was checked via the Steam news API, and none has shipped [src:steam-2023-cmbs-update-2-18].
- **Developer countries still unverified**: Sand Table Software (the store page and the studio site give none), Bird's Eye Games (Regiments), Cats Who Play (Gostomel Heroes), Ravens Row (Hell Of War) and Battlestate Games (Escape from Tarkov). Death From Above's makers are confirmed German.
- **ADB values before April 2025** beyond the infantry price, and the exact date of the 6→12 repricing, which falls between April 2025 and January 2026.
- Why *Gostomel Heroes* is missing from the Ukrainian and German Steam stores (regional withdrawal, rating or developer choice) is not established.
- The *Play for Ukraine* full text (Taylor & Francis) returns 403. Only its abstract and metadata were read.
## 11. Sources

- **Standards family.** NATO APP-6 (STANAG 2019) and US MIL-STD-2525 are aligned standards. APP-6A (1999) is equivalent to MIL-STD-2525A. Later editions are APP-6B (2008) and APP-6C (2011), and APP-6E is listed as current [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology]. milsymbol supports MIL-STD-2525C/D/E, FM 1-02.2 and APP-6 B/D/E [src:github-milsymbol].
- **Affiliation is encoded twice, by frame shape and by colour** [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology]:
  - **Friend:** rectangle, **blue**
  - **Hostile:** diamond, **red**
  - **Neutral:** square, **green**
  - **Unknown:** quatrefoil, **yellow**
  - Further states: pending, assumed friend, suspect, and exercise variants.
  - Because the shape carries affiliation too, symbols work in monochrome.
- **Frame modifiers** [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology]:
  - Solid frame = present; **dashed frame = planned/anticipated**.
  - Closed frames = land and sea surface; bottom-open = air/space; top-open = subsurface.
- **Symbol anatomy** [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology] [src:spatialillusions-battle-staff-tools]:
  - Frame, central icon, optional fill.
  - Modifiers/amplifiers arranged around the frame: unique designation, additional information, altitude/depth, combat effectiveness, headquarters/task force/dummy, echelon/mobility.
- **Echelons.** Coded in the SIDC and drawn above the frame: Team/Crew, Squad, Section, Platoon/detachment, Company/battery/troop, Battalion/squadron, Regiment/group, Brigade, Division, Corps, Army, Army Group/front, Region/Theatre, Command [src:github-milsymbol].
- **SIDC formats.** Older standards use letter-based symbol identification codes, 15 characters in the APP-6A lineage [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology]. Current 2525D/E and APP-6D/E use numeric codes; milsymbol's README example is a 30-digit SIDC. milsymbol implements both schemes [src:github-milsymbol].
- **Renderers:**
  - **milsymbol** (Måns Beckman / spatialillusions):
    - Pure JavaScript, **MIT licence**, SVG or Canvas output.
    - Filled/unfilled and framed/unframed symbols, text fields, movement indicators.
    - Since v3.0 it renders to MIL-STD-2525E/APP-6E appearance for every SIDC version. The latest release is v3.0.4 (March 2026).
    - Integrations include Leaflet, OpenLayers and Cesium [src:github-milsymbol].
    - This is the safe choice for game assets, e.g. pre-render SVGs to a texture atlas at build time.
  - **Spatial Illusions "Battle Staff Tools"** (the "unit generator"):
    - A browser tool for MIL-STD-2525E/APP-6E and 2525C/APP-6B symbols with PNG/SVG export, ORBAT building and a map.
    - © 2025 Måns Beckman. Free on spatialillusions.com with watermarks and donation prompts; offline use or use on other sites needs a paid licence file [src:spatialillusions-battle-staff-tools].
    - Treat its exports as **not** cleared for redistribution in a game.
- **Who follows NATO conventions:**
  - Black Bird Group explicitly uses the NATO convention "red is the Russian adversary, blue is Ukrainian" [src:blackbirdgroup-map].
  - Delta was "built according to NATO standards" [src:militarnyi-2022-delta-unveiled].
  - DeepState does not use APP-6 frames [src:deepstate-api-history].
### e9-counteroffensive-26 (Feb 2026–present)

- **Artillery, HIMARS and glide bombs in Vivaldi and the southern counteroffensive.** No source quantifies them. Vivaldi was run under "maximum information silence", and the ISW special report and daily assessments (read via Wayback) describe drone-led shaping fires, not tube fire. A later RUSI fieldwork report is the likeliest source.
- **Per-town KAB counts.** Avdiivka (February 2024) is sourced. Vovchansk has only qualitative reporting, and Kharkiv city only a strike count (more than 50 by mid-June 2024). ISW assessments from May–June 2024 via Wayback had no per-town numbers.
- **KAB monthly series gaps.** February 2026 is derived (March minus "more than 1,500"). Most 2024 and 2025 months are missing; only April–May 2024, early 2025, October and November 2025 are sourced. A full Air Force/MoD series was not found in English.
- **Artillery's share of casualties.** Only the complement is sourced: drones cause 70–80% (Latvian SAB), and more than 80% of targets destroyed (UA MoD). No source splits the remaining 20–30% between artillery, glide bombs, mines and small arms.
- **Conflicting production figures.** RUSI's 70,000 UMPK ordered for 2025 against HUR's 120,000 planned. Actual drops (~44,000 in Jan–Nov 2025) suggest stockpiling or overstated plans. Flamingo's maker claims (30–210 a month) are contradicted by the strike record (~10 strikes). Sapsan's production is unverified.
- **Czech initiative totals.** Pavel's figures differ between February 2026 (4.4M cumulative, almost 2M in 2025) and May 2026 (just over 3M: 1.5M plus 1.8M). The difference may be calibre scope (122 mm included) or counting method.
- **Interceptor-drone kill share.** Official counts conflict (USF: over 1,200 in May 2026; Sting's maker: over 3,000), and the Air Force stopped publishing Shahed counts from May 2026. Cost per kill is only implied (a ~$2k interceptor against a $20–50k Shahed); file 01 has the detail.
- **Ballistic intercept methodology.** CSIS, the MoD monthly and Air Force per-salvo figures are now all sourced, but none separates PAC-3 from SAMP/T or counts interceptors fired per kill.

**Peace talks and ceasefires.**
- **Abu Dhabi, second round (4–5 Feb 2026):** a 314-person exchange and no ceasefire. A short energy-strike moratorium was in force at the time [src:isw-2026-02-05-roca].
- **Geneva (17–18 Feb):** talks failed on Donbas [src:kyivindependent-2026-fenbert-300km].
- **Orthodox Easter truce (11–13 Apr 2026):** 32 hours from 16:00 on 11 Apr. The General Staff logged 10,721 Russian violations. Long-range strikes paused for about a day, but artillery, FPVs and assaults did not [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-easter-truce]. Pass 1's figure of 469 violations, taken from Wikipedia, is superseded.
- **Victory Day.** Ukraine declared a unilateral ceasefire from 6 May, which Russia ignored [src:isw-2026-05-06-roca]. Both sides then agreed a **9–11 May** ceasefire with a POW exchange. The Kremlin restated that Ukraine must withdraw from the rest of Donetsk Oblast before any ceasefire [src:isw-2026-05-08-roca]. Limited fighting went on, and Russia used the pause to rotate and resupply [src:isw-2026-05-09-roca].
- **The envoys' visit (5–8 Sep).**
  - Kyiv and Moscow halted long-range strikes on each other's capitals from 5 to 7 Sep.
  - Ukrainian brigades were ordered to hold fire along the front from 5 to 8 Sep, a truce Ukraine proposed and Putin rejected [src:isw-2026-09-05-roca].
  - On 6 Sep Zelensky and Witkoff/Kushner agreed "fundamental principles", including security and economic guarantees, while Putin restated maximalist aims [src:isw-2026-09-06-roca].
  - Sources differ on the outcome: CSMonitor reports that Zelensky rejected the plan's terms [src:csmonitor-2026-weir-peace-talks].
- **"Energy ceasefire" (14 Sep):** Trump announced a mutual halt to energy strikes. Zelensky offered one on condition of reciprocity, and Russia did not respond [src:isw-2026-09-14-roca]. By 25 Sep Putin was signalling a winter strike campaign instead [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].

markdown:
Night, fog and rain reduce drone effectiveness; this is when rotations and infiltration happen. Scale the depth up by era, from about 3 km (2023) to 25+ km (2026). Sources: rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments, pravda-2026-levytska-magyar-kill-zone.
- **Detection → strike latency as a core stat.**
  - About 3–5 minutes with an organic drone; 20–30 minutes through an HQ; hours to days at operational level (2022–23).
  - Ukrainian digital tools (GIS Arta at 30–45 s, Avengers detection at 2.2 s) shorten the loop.
  - Loss of a C2 bearer (Starlink-cutoff event, EW) lengthens it and can cause friendly fire.
  - 2025–26 figures are thin and not independent. Russia's Glaz/Groza cut its drone-to-artillery loop "from hours to minutes" (CSIS, from Russian developer channels). Euromaidan Press says Delta cut Ukraine's detection-to-strike time "from roughly 20 minutes to a few" (unattributed). RUSI gives slower timings for everything else: 24–48 hours for each of the first three attack phases, and 2–3 hours from UGV rendezvous to medical post [src:csis-2026-bondar-russian-c2] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-hryfon-zakhid] [src:rusi-2025-watling-combined-arms].

- **Ukrainian offence.** Kherson began on 29 August 2022 and drew in Russian reserves. Kharkiv followed on a thinly held front: Ukraine did not surprise Russia about its intentions, but did surprise it on timing [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. Ukraine advanced 75 km in four days (Balakliia, Izium, Kupiansk) against a Russian defence of "one tier" [src:euromaidan-2022-shandra-kharkiv]. At Kherson, Russia withdrew in good order across the Dnipro in October–November [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Russian response.** Russia declared mobilization, took the Dnipro as a barrier, and began building deliberate defence lines (the "Surovikin line") in Zaporizhzhia. By May 2023 its group of forces was about 420,000 strong [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**What Russia had.** Wagner plus mobilised convicts, with VDV support. **19,547 Wagner fighters killed in Bakhmut**, 88% of them convicts, and a similar number seriously wounded. Russia also held a **5:1 artillery advantage** [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. By Mar 2023, prisoners were the largest category in Mediazona's count of named Russian dead [src:mediazona-2026-casualties-count].
## 9. Terms

- **Russian assault style.** Meatgrinder describes a four-tier infantry system:
  - Disposable infantry came from DNR/LNR conscripts, Wagner convicts and under-trained mobilized men. They were first organised in companies of about 60, later in platoons of about 15, and attacked in fire teams of 2–5, with up to 5 teams on one axis.
  - The teams skirmished "often until killed". Some were shot by their own side when retreating, and Ukrainian troops report many appeared to be on amphetamines.
  - Specialised and assault troops were then sent against the Ukrainian positions this exposed [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
  - At Artemivske in December 2022, four UAVs flew over each assault group, covering reconnaissance, reserve routes, ambush detection and the commander's view.
- **Losses.** 19,547 Wagner fighters were killed at Bakhmut and a similar number seriously wounded. 88% of them were convicts; trained Wagner deaths averaged 40–60 a week. About 10,000 Ukrainians were killed or severely wounded in and around the city, and Russia held a 5:1 artillery advantage [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Russian penal units.** Storm-Z convict companies in regular units offered a pardon after six months and ended in August 2023. From late 2023 they were replaced by Storm-V, with no pardon and contracts lasting until the end of the war [src:ukrpravda-2024-isw-storm-v].
- **Vuhledar.** The ill-prepared January–February 2023 offensive "beginning in Vuhledar" was extremely costly. The Russian command appears to have judged it could "trade lives for time" [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Ukrainian defence.** Ukraine lost about 10,000 UAVs a month to Russian EW [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Ukrainian losses turned unfavourable once Russian artillery controlled the roads into Bakhmut [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**Command change.** Defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov was sacked in mid-July, which set off street protests. Special-operations commander Yevhen Khmara became acting minister on 16 Jul [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-khmara]. On 21 Jul Maj Gen **Mykhailo Drapatyi** replaced Syrskyi as Commander-in-Chief. Zelensky said the mid- and long-range strike programmes would continue unchanged [src:guardian-2026-murray-drapatyi].

markdown: ## 9. Terms

**What Ukraine had.** Pre-war stocks, plus rapid Western light anti-armour and MANPADS deliveries (Javelin, NLAW, Stinger) and Bayraktar TB2s. US deliveries over the whole war reached more than 10,000 Javelins, 10,000 TOWs and 3,000 Stingers, but the fact sheet gives totals rather than arrival dates [src:state-2025-us-security-cooperation-ukraine]. Ukraine kept **artillery parity for about the first six weeks**, until its ammunition ran short [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. "From April, the West became Ukraine's strategic depth" [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. The first Western 155 mm guns arrived at the very end of the era: Canada announced its M777s delivered on 23 Apr 2022, "in conjunction with our American Allies" [src:ukrinform-2022-canada-m777].

markdown:
- The Orlan-10 was the Russian workhorse. Russian units with their own UAVs could fire within 3–5 minutes of detection, against 20–30 minutes when the request went through a fire-control headquarters. Even so, Russia did not have enough Orlans to sustain its loss rate in Donbas [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Army of Drones** (Armiia Droniv) launched in July 2022, run by UNITED24, the General Staff and the Ministry of Digital Transformation. Within 9 months it had contracted 3,200 UAV complexes (over UAH 4bn, about $107m) and trained 7,000+ operators [src:pravda-2023-fedorov-army-of-drones].

Per era (computed net Russian change): e2 (May–Aug 2022) +3,782; e3 (Sep–Nov 2022) −17,533, with 18,256 recaptured; e4 (Dec 2022–May 2023) +703; e5 (Jun–Nov 2023) −441; e6 (Dec 2023–Jul 2024) +989, about 124 a month; e7 (Aug 2024–Mar 2025) +3,037, about 380 a month; e8 (Apr 2025–Jan 2026) +3,928, about 393 a month; e9 (Feb–Sep 2026) +620, about 78 a month, against 444 km² recaptured. Russian-held territory including the pre-2022 zone rose from 107,553 km² (end 2022) to 116,195 km² (27 Sep 2026), about 19.3% of Ukraine; DeepState's own total at the end of 2025 was 116,165 km² against the computed 115,330 [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-2025-4336]. The routed Radio Svoboda figures (450–550 km² a month at the 2025 peak, 27 in July 2026) fit the series for May–Aug 2025 (439–564) but not for July 2026, where DeepState's own report and the computation both give 36 [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km].

**Defining features.** Russia's firepower-driven attrition against a Ukraine short of ammunition. Glide bombs "gave the VKS teeth" without air superiority [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].

- **DeepStateMap is the reference.** It is Ukrainian, run by the DeepState UA NGO, fed largely by Ukrainian military sources, and deliberately published 2–3 days late for operational security [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping]. Its visual grammar is simple. Semi-transparent area fills show control status (occupied, liberated, recently liberated, unknown/grey, pre-2022 occupied). Point icons mark Russian units, airfields and HQs, and arrows show "directions of attack" [src:deepstate-api-history]. Ukrainian positions are never shown [src:kyivpost-2025-ashcroft-inside-deepstate].
- **ISW/CTP is the Western reference.** Its legend is epistemic rather than just territorial. It separates *assessed* (evidence-backed) from *claimed* (asserted, unverified) and, since December 2025, draws a dedicated *infiltration areas* layer [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain]. Most Western outlets (e.g., the BBC) redraw ISW/CTP data [src:bbc-2022-ukraine-in-maps].
- **The front line has stopped being a line.** From 2025 on, drone "kill zones" and infiltration by small Russian groups turned the grey zone from a thin no-man's-land into a deep contact zone with overlapping positions. That forced DeepState (2026) and ISW (Dec 2025) to redefine their uncertainty categories [src:onlineua-2026-deepstate-legend] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping] [src:warontherocks-2026-maurin-front-line]. This is directly relevant to eras e8-drone-kill-zone and e9-counteroffensive-26.
- **Mapping is political.** DeepState has clashed publicly with Ukrainian commanders over encirclements and breakthroughs (Makarivka, Dec 2024; Dobropillia, Aug 2025). Flag-planting photo-ops by both sides are an information-war tactic that careful mappers refuse to map [src:devua-2024-deepstate-makarivka] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping].
- **Tactical UIs are a different world.** Delta (MoD situational awareness), Kropyva (Army SOS artillery/mapping tablet app), and the "Vezha" drone-stream module with Avengers AI are the Ukrainian military's own digital layers [src:wikipedia-delta] [src:militarnyi-2022-delta-unveiled] [src:forbes-2022-hambling-kropyva]. The Army of Drones Bonus "e-points" system turned video-verified strikes into a points economy with unit leaderboards and a marketplace [src:kyivpost-2026-korshak-epoints] [src:defensenews-2026-ruitenberg-epoints] [src:united24-2026-petriv-army-of-drones].
- **One consistent territory metric exists.** DeepState's undocumented history endpoint serves the full GeoJSON of every map version since 3 April 2022. Differencing month-end versions reproduces DeepState's own published monthly figures to within a few km² in most months, and gives Russian gains and Ukrainian recaptures separately (§2.7) [src:deepstate-api-history] [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-2025-4336].
- **Data rights are the main blocker.** DeepState has no documented API or open licence, although undocumented JSON endpoints exist and community scrapers use them. ISW's ArcGIS layers are public but carry "exclusive intellectual property… written consent" terms. ACLED requires a corporate licence for commercial use [src:deepstate-api-history] [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain] [src:acled-eula]. GeoConfirmed's free API is scoped to "research, journalism, and analytical use", and Liveuamap allows reuse "with reference" but sells its API [src:geoconfirmed-openapi] [src:liveuamap-about-terms]. Only the symbology renderer milsymbol is permissively (MIT) licensed [src:github-milsymbol].

- **Kill-zone depth by era.** Model drone threat as a band with a density gradient that deepens over time:
  - 2022: sparse and short-range.
  - 2024: dense to about 3 km, thinning to 15 km, taskable to 40 km [src:rusi-2025-watling-reynolds-third-year].
  - 2025: 10–15 km lethal, with fiber-optic FPVs and Molniya reaching 40–50 km [src:ukrinform-2025-fedorov-fiber-optic-40km][src:mezha-2026-molniya].
  - 2026: 20–25 km on active axes, with 30 km expected by year-end [src:euromaidanpress-2026-vivdych-kill-zone-corps].

- **Russian shell economy.** In Q1 2023 Russia fired 12,000–38,000 rounds a day, and days above 24,000 became rare. Use shifted from 152 mm guns to 120 mm mortars. Annual consumption was trending to about 7M against Ukrainian estimates of about 2.5M a year in Russian production [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
- **Russian reconnaissance-fire circuit (the Russian term for the kill chain).** Each axis commander keeps Orlan-10 orbits overhead, and the artillery brigade flies its own complex. Engagement takes about 3–5 min from UAV detection and 20–30 min from EW detection. The Strelets system links sensors to digital fire control. Krasnopol laser-guided shells and Lancet loitering munitions do counter-battery work and hunt guns [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
- **Russian air defence** now intercepts a share of GMLRS [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Excalibur's confirmed hit rate fell from more than 55% early in 2023 to 7% in July and 6% in August 2023. JDAM-ER, delivered from February 2023, lost accuracy within weeks, and a patch followed in May 2023 [src:stripes-2024-khurshudyan-jamming].
- **The VKS stays stand-off.** It uses FAB-500s with early glide kits from Su-35S out to about 70 km, in small but steady numbers, plus lofted S-8. Industry supplies about 40 long-range missiles a month. Tu-95 packages use Shaheds as pathfinders to find gaps in Ukrainian air defence [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
